newsitem.title: FRANCE: Socialists charge Chirac caved in to Kohl on EMU.
newsitem.headline: Socialists charge Chirac caved in to Kohl on EMU.

text.p: France's opposition Socialist Party accused President Jacques Chirac on Wednesday of caving in to Germany on a "stability pact" to bar overspending by members of a future single European currency.

"On the stability pact, the French government has accepted the German position and the only remaining discussion is about details of the financial sanctions," Socialist spokesman Francois Hollande told reporters.

Under the pact proposed by German Finance Minister Theo Waigel, countries which exceeded a budget deficit of three percent of gross domestic product after monetary union would be subject of automatic fines of up to 0.5 percent of GDP.

Hollande said the Socialists were worried that France had not made its own line clear on these issues either at a Franco-German summit in Nuremberg on Monday or in advance of Friday's European Union summit in Dublin.
"It is because there is no clear line that the European integration process is stagnating today or deviating towards principles which seem unacceptable to us, notably the stability pact," he said.

Bank of France Governor Jean-Claude Trichet was quoted on Wednesday as saying he had "no doubt" European countries would iron out differences and agree on a stability pact to enforce fiscal discipline under monetary union.
He said hard bargaining over Germany's call for automatic penalties for countries which violate the Maastricht treaty's tight fiscal limits after 1999 was a matter "of definition".

"We all support, in certain cases, fines against budget sinners for the sake of the euro's stability. We just have to decide when sanctions should apply automatically and when a political judgement is needed," Trichet told the German weekly Die Zeit.
